items.html:
Governing Features: NumPy-compatible lattice input forms, analytic first-order autodiff, native memory-error handling, and precision-preserving Torch inputs.

Feature Fit: The changes address those contracts, except one incomplete lattice normalization path.

Behavior Model: Framework inputs are normalized before native callbacks; native pullbacks must match every normalized input’s shape.

Bug Candidates:

  • [P2][bug] Raw larger cells are not reduced before differentiation — _lattice.py:531–535. Calling solve_periodic with a traced three-element diagonal such as [0.9, 0.95, 1.1] and kpar=[0, 0] infers a two-dimensional cell but leaves the diagonal unchanged. The native callback subsequently selects its 2×2 sublattice, producing a (2,2) lattice gradient for the (3,) framework input. Backward raises a gradient-shape ValueError; the retained lattice also prevents to_smatrix from recognizing the two-dimensional cell. Root reproduced this failure. Normalize and select the sublattice within the framework before invoking the record, preserving Lattice._sublattice separability and row-selection behavior. This closes an existing gap in the newly expanded normalization path; it is not a newly introduced regression.

Invariant Risks: The proposed fix must preserve row-permuted separable lattices; _sublattice selects rows by their nonzero requested components.

Fail-Fast Violations: No additional findings.

Compatibility Risks: No additional findings.

No Findings: No independent defects found in the changed Torch conversion, coordinate rejection, angle conversion, one-dimensional broadcasting, or fallible diffraction-order allocation. Read-only review only; tests and builds were not run.

No remaining correctness findings in 86c4b2d..f1fae3e.

The fix normalizes larger cells before the native callback, preserves Lattice._sublattice validation and row ordering, and returns gradients with the original input shape. One-dimensional sum broadcasting remains unchanged. New tests cover all four backends, row-permuted cells, and zero gradients for excluded axes.

Read-only review; I did not run tests or builds. The 674 passing tests and memory-error results are root-reported evidence.
